prompts.text: What are you avoiding by staying busy — and what would you find if you stopped?

connections.title: Cultivate practical judgment (gnome)

prompts.text: What is the smallest good thing in the room right now?

connections.title: Make eudaimonia the organising end of your life

prompts.text: What are you deliberating about that you've already decided?

connections.title: Understand that you are responsible for your character

prompts.text: Which friendship would survive a change in circumstance — and which wouldn't?

prompts.text: What is the pleasure that costs more than it gives?

connections.title: Practice resilience in adversity

connections.title: Practice truthfulness (aletheia)

connections.title: Relation is primary

prompts.text: What are you doing right now that would be different if you were only doing that?

connections.title: Cultivate single-tasking — do one thing at a time

prompts.text: What are you taking that was never offered — someone's time, attention, or credit?

connections.title: Take only what is given

connections.title: Practice generosity (eleutheriotes)
connections.why: Generosity is the same line drawn from the giving side.

prompts.text: What did you make this month that would not have existed otherwise?

connections.title: Create as growth — creation is the evidence of growth

connections.title: Practise meaning through creative work
connections.why: Frankl's first route: making something that matters.

prompts.text: What is the story you tell about why your life matters — and does it hold together?

connections.title: Build narrative coherence
connections.why: Coherence is what the story is missing when it breaks.

prompts.text: What would you do differently if the daily work were the thing itself, not the means to it?

connections.title: Practise Sisyphus happy

connections.title: Make activities autotelic — worth doing for their own sake

prompts.text: When did the budget of your attention fit together — and what was that like?

connections.title: Practise leisure (scholē) as the end of work

prompts.text: What has actually been changing in your relationships, rest, and willingness over the last months?

connections.title: The good life is a process, not a state

connections.title: Judge your life as a direction, not a destination

prompts.text: Which of your goals is actually someone else's — and whose?

prompts.text: What is the future self you fear becoming — and what is one behavior that feeds it?

connections.title: Recognise that goal progress predicts well-being — pursuing goals is good for you

prompts.text: Which outcome, if it went badly, would you take as a verdict on your worth?

connections.why: Notice the move from judgment about work to judgment about your value.

connections.title: Learn to distinguish self-worth from performance
connections.why: The distinction is the whole practice.

prompts.text: What is the sentence you keep saying about yourself — and who is the one saying it?

connections.title: Distinguish the observing self from the story of self

connections.title: Recognise the observing self — you are not only the contents of awareness

prompts.text: What is the one word for what your mind is doing right now?

connections.title: Bring the mind back, without drama

prompts.text: What does your breath feel like at the nostrils — right now?

connections.title: Practice mindfulness of breathing (anapanasati)

prompts.text: What are you feeling precisely — not 'bad', but what?

connections.title: Learn the structure of your affect — valence and arousal
connections.why: Valence and arousal is the first cut.

connections.title: Do not add to the impression

connections.why: The wider range is the point of the exercise.

prompts.text: When did something vast make your to-do list feel small — and what did you do with that?

connections.title: Recognise the restorative power of awe — vastness expands attention

connections.title: Cultivate hope — it is not wishful thinking; it is agency plus pathway

connections.title: Learn to disengage from unattainable goals — letting go is adaptive
connections.why: Sometimes the missing piece is releasing the goal, not finding the route.

prompts.text: What are you angry about — and what happened versus what you inferred?

connections.title: Recognise guilt's adaptive function — it motivates repair

connections.title: Practice recognizing the kindness you have received
connections.why: Recognition is gratitude's specific form.

connections.title: Recognise motivation and culture — motivational ideals vary

connections.why: The ledger entries are instructions; take it down when you need direction.

connections.title: Practise gratitude with specificity
connections.why: One line, concrete, is the format.

connections.title: Cultivate good deliberation (euboulia)

connections.title: The good life is a process, not a state

connections.title: Practice patience with others' faults

connections.title: Create as growth — creation is the evidence of growth

connections.title: Recognise that virtue is a hexis, not a feeling

connections.title: Learn to make habits small — start tiny

connections.title: Practise perceptiveness (aisthesis)
connections.why: The trained eye comes from staying, not from scanning.

prompts.text: What would you not change about your life, backwards or forwards?

connections.title: Practise amor fati
connections.why: The wish is that you would not change what had to be.

connections.title: Practise the eternal recurrence
connections.why: The recurrence question is amor fati's stress test.

prompts.text: What conversation are you rehearsing instead of having?

connections.title: Take committed action — behavior is where values become real
connections.why: The rehearsal is where the value goes to hide.

connections.title: Reconcile quickly — don't let conflict fester
connections.why: The rehearsal is the festering in disguise.

prompts.text: What coal are you holding — and for whom is the release?

connections.title: Forgive — release the coal
connections.why: The image is the whole teaching: the coal is yours.

connections.title: Forgive those who wrong you
connections.why: The Stoic line agrees on the mechanism, not the sentiment.

prompts.text: What is the state of your mind right now — and could you name it without a verdict?

connections.title: Watch states arise and pass
connections.why: The naming is the watching; the verdict is extra.

connections.title: Note lightly (noting)
connections.why: One word, at the moment, and back.

prompts.text: What is the work you would do even if the book never sells?

connections.title: Value the process over the outcome
connections.why: Writing every morning because you like it, whether or not it sells.

connections.title: Make activities autotelic — worth doing for their own sake
connections.why: The external benefits set aside, the doing still recommends itself.

prompts.text: Where are you trying to convince — and where would dropping the need work better?

connections.title: Drop the need to convince
connections.why: The need to convince is often the obstacle to being heard.

connections.title: Practise critical distance
connections.why: Distance from your own position is where the convincing ends.

prompts.text: What are you a peer slightly ahead of someone on — and could you be taught by the one ahead of you?

connections.title: Treat social comparison as a double-edged sword
connections.why: A peer slightly ahead on the same road is a comparison that can teach.

connections.title: Practice generosity (eleutheriotes)
connections.why: Being the one ahead carries its own duty.

prompts.text: What one thing could you give your full attention to for its own duration?

connections.title: Wash the dishes to wash the dishes
connections.why: One act at a time is the whole instruction.

connections.title: Cultivate single-tasking — do one thing at a time
connections.why: Single-tasking is the attentional form of the same.

prompts.text: Whose trouble did you sit with today without fixing?

connections.title: Practice sending and taking on the breath
connections.why: The direction is deliberate: take in the bad, send out the good.

connections.title: Practice gentleness (praotes)
connections.why: Gentleness is often the not-fixing.

prompts.text: What is the thing you do at a set time whether or not insight shows up?

connections.title: Make self-study a discipline
connections.why: Attendance, not inspiration.

connections.title: Make habit your flywheel
connections.why: The flywheel doesn't ask for the mood.

prompts.text: What are you seeing in your friend that you are not seeing in yourself?

connections.title: Recognise the self-serving bias — you take credit for success and blame failure on circumstances
connections.why: The bias runs opposite directions for self and other.

connections.title: Recognize your blindness — others live in worlds you cannot see
connections.why: The blindness is structural, not personal.

prompts.text: What do you want from the promotion — and what are you trying to avoid?

connections.title: Expect fluctuation, and read it as structure
connections.why: Both sentences describe the same choice; neither is the answer alone.

connections.title: Recognise mastery vs performance goals — learning vs proving
connections.why: The promotion can be either, depending on the sentence.

prompts.text: What restlessness in you needs a walk rather than a judgment?

connections.title: Use antidotes skillfully
connections.why: Restlessness gets a walk; the moralist's question is the wrong one.

connections.title: Learn that walking is underrated — simple, accessible, effective
connections.why: The walk is both the antidote and the evidence.

prompts.text: What did you make this week that a burst of inspiration wouldn't have produced?

connections.title: Make self-study a discipline
connections.why: The notebook holds a year of the mind; no burst would have.

connections.title: Create as growth — creation is the evidence of growth
connections.why: The evidence is the output, not the feeling.

prompts.text: What did you say yes to that you would rather have declined — and did they have room?

connections.title: Keep your intentions transparent
connections.why: Ask plainly and leave them room to decline — including yourself.

connections.title: Learn assertiveness — express needs and boundaries directly
connections.why: Declining is assertiveness too.

prompts.text: What distraction did you catch today — and was the catch the practice?

connections.title: Practise deliberate distraction management — know what pulls your attention
connections.why: Knowing what pulls is the first catch.

connections.title: Learn to redirect attention after distraction — the return, not the absence of distraction, is the skill
connections.why: The catch is the return, not the absence.

prompts.text: What would you do if you trusted that the mind is trainable?

connections.title: Trust that the mind is trainable
connections.why: The trust is the premise of every practice here.

connections.title: Recognise that attention is trainable — it can be cultivated
connections.why: Cultivation is the claim; the rest is agriculture.

prompts.text: What feeling are you having — rather than being?

connections.title: Recognise the observing self — you are not only the contents of awareness
connections.why: 'There is panic' instead of 'I am panic' — grammar-sized, freedom-large.

connections.title: Learn to let affect pass — feelings are impermanent
connections.why: The feeling is a weather report, not an identity.

prompts.text: What do you believe that you have never asked for the cash value of?

connections.title: Ask for the cash value of your beliefs
connections.why: Peirce's question: what would the belief do differently?

connections.title: An idea's meaning is its practical effects
connections.why: The meaning is the effects, not the statement.

prompts.text: What is enough for today — and what would 'enough' look like written down?

connections.title: Know what is enough (zhizu)
connections.why: Enough is a knowable number, not a feeling.

connections.title: Learn to manage perfectionism — good enough enables action
connections.why: Define done before starting; ship at that threshold.

prompts.text: What would you do with the last day of a life you were not wishing were different?

connections.title: Practise amor fati
connections.why: Not wishing the life that includes it were a different life.

connections.title: Do not postpone living well
connections.why: Postponement is the wish in action.
